notes.summary: History gives about 3 to 4 questions in Tier 1 and more in Tier 2. In past papers the modern period (British rule, Congress, Gandhi, revolutionaries) gives the most questions, then the Mughals and Delhi Sultanate, then the Guptas and Mauryas. Learn each fact as a pair: person and work, place and event, year and event. For order questions, write the year next to each event first.

concepts.title: Stone Age, Indus Valley and Vedic age
concepts.body:
Stone Age sites: Bhimbetka rock shelters (Madhya Pradesh, Palaeolithic paintings, UNESCO site); Mehrgarh (Pakistan, early farming); Burzahom (Kashmir, pit houses). A celt is a polished stone axe of the Neolithic period.

Indus siteWhereRemember for
HarappaRavi river, Punjab (Pakistan)First excavated, Daya Ram Sahni, 1921; granaries
Mohenjo-daroIndus river, Sindh (Pakistan)R.D. Banerji, 1922; Great Bath, bronze dancing girl, 'priest-king'
LothalGujaratDockyard, port city; excavated by S.R. Rao
KalibanganGhaggar river, RajasthanPloughed field, fire altars
DholaviraKutch, GujaratWater reservoirs, large signboard; UNESCO site (2021)
RakhigarhiHaryanaLargest Harappan site in India
ChanhudaroSindh (Pakistan)Bead-making; city without a citadel

Vedic age (about 1500 to 600 BC): the early Vedic people lived in the land of seven rivers (Sapta Sindhu). The Rigveda is the oldest Veda: 10 mandalas, 1028 hymns; it has the Gayatri Mantra and the first mention of the Bharata tribe and the Battle of Ten Kings. Sama Veda: hymns set to music. Yajur Veda: sacrificial formulas. Atharva Veda: charms, spells and medicine. 'Satyameva Jayate' comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.

Six Vedangas: Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (word origins), Chhanda (metre), Jyotisha (astronomy).

concepts.title: Mahajanapadas, Buddhism and Jainism
concepts.body:
In the 6th century BC there were 16 Mahajanapadas (listed in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya). Assaka was the only one in the south (on the Godavari).

MahajanapadaCapital
MagadhaRajagriha (Girivraja), later Pataliputra
KosalaShravasti
VatsaKaushambi
AvantiUjjayini (Ujjain)
AngaChampa
KashiVaranasi
VajjiVaishali
GandharaTaxila
SurasenaMathura

Magadha's dynasties: Haryanka (Bimbisara, Ajatashatru; Udayin founded Pataliputra), Shishunaga, then Nanda (Mahapadma Nanda, Dhana Nanda). Alexander invaded in 326 BC and fought Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum).

Buddha: born at Lumbini (Nepal) in the Shakya clan; enlightenment at Bodh Gaya; first sermon at Sarnath (Dharmachakra Pravartana); death (mahaparinirvana) at Kushinagar. Texts: Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma), in Pali.

Buddhist councilPlaceKing
FirstRajagrihaAjatashatru
SecondVaishaliKalashoka
ThirdPataliputraAshoka
FourthKashmirKanishka (split into Hinayana and Mahayana)

Jainism: Rishabhanatha was the 1st tirthankara, Parshvanatha the 23rd, Mahavira the 24th (born at Kundagrama near Vaishali, died at Pawapuri). 'Jina' means the conqueror (of the senses). Three jewels (triratna): right faith, right knowledge, right conduct. Two sects: Svetambara (white-clad) and Digambara (sky-clad).

concepts.title: Mauryas and after
concepts.body:
• Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire (about 321 BC) with Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra. Megasthenes, envoy of Seleucus, wrote Indica. Chandragupta became a Jain and died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka).
  • Bindusara was called Amitraghata (slayer of foes).
  • Ashoka fought the Kalinga war (about 261 BC) and then followed Dhamma. Most edicts are in Prakrit in the Brahmi script; the north-west ones are in Kharosthi. James Prinsep read the Brahmi script in 1837. The Lion Capital at Sarnath is India's national emblem. Ashoka built the original Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh) and stupas at Sarnath.
  • The last Mauryan king Brihadratha was killed by his general Pushyamitra Shunga, who founded the Shunga dynasty.
Post-Mauryan powerRemember for
SatavahanasDeccan; founder Simuka; Gautamiputra Satakarni
Indo-GreeksMenander (Milinda), who questioned Nagasena in Milindapanho; first gold coins in India
ShakasRudradaman's Junagadh inscription, the first long inscription in Sanskrit
KushanasKanishka; Shaka era starts 78 AD; capitals Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura; Gandhara and Mathura schools of art
Kharavela (Kalinga)Hathigumpha inscription, Udayagiri (Odisha)

concepts.title: Guptas and Harsha
concepts.body:
RulerRemember for
Sri GuptaFounder
Chandragupta IBegan the Gupta era (320 AD); married the Licchavi princess Kumaradevi
SamudraguptaAllahabad Pillar inscription (Prayag Prashasti) by his poet Harishena; called the 'Napoleon of India' by V.A. Smith; coins show him playing the veena
Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)Defeated the Shakas; Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited; Kalidasa was in his court (navaratnas)
Kumaragupta IFounded Nalanda university
SkandaguptaPushed back the Huns

The Gupta period is called the 'Golden Age'. Aryabhata wrote Aryabhatiya; Varahamihira wrote Brihat Samhita; Kalidasa wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta and Raghuvamsha.

Harshavardhana (606 to 647 AD) ruled from Thanesar and then Kannauj. The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) described his assemblies at Kannauj and Prayag. Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita; Harsha himself wrote the plays Ratnavali, Nagananda and Priyadarshika. He was defeated on the Narmada by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II.

Foreign writers: Megasthenes (Indica, Maurya), Pliny the Elder (Natural History, Roman), Ptolemy (Geography), Fa-Hien (Chandragupta II), Hiuen Tsang (Harsha), Al-Biruni (Kitab-ul-Hind, came with Mahmud of Ghazni).

concepts.title: South India and the Deccan
concepts.body:
KingdomCapitalRemember for
Sangam Cheras, Cholas, PandyasVanji, Uraiyur (Puhar port), MaduraiSangam literature in Tamil; Pandyas held the Sangam assemblies at Madurai
PallavasKanchipuramRathas at Mahabalipuram (Narasimhavarman I 'Mamalla'); Shore Temple
Chalukyas of BadamiVatapi (Badami)Pulakeshin II; Aihole inscription by Ravikirti
RashtrakutasManyakhetaFounder Dantidurga; Krishna I built the Kailasa temple, Ellora; Amoghavarsha wrote Kavirajamarga (Kannada)
Cholas (imperial)Thanjavur, later GangaikondacholapuramVijayalaya founder; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara temple; Rajendra I took the title 'Gangaikondachola' and sent a navy to South-East Asia; Uttaramerur inscriptions on village assemblies

Tripartite struggle for Kannauj (8th to 10th century): Palas (Bengal), Gurjara-Pratiharas (western India) and Rashtrakutas (Deccan). Pala founder Gopala; Dharmapala founded Vikramashila university.

Vijayanagara: founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka (Sangama dynasty); capital Hampi on the Tungabhadra (Karnataka). Four dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu. Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva) wrote Amuktamalyada (Telugu, also on statecraft); his court poets were the Ashtadiggajas. The empire was crushed at the Battle of Talikota (1565).

Bahmani kingdom: founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah; capitals Gulbarga, then Bidar. Minister Mahmud Gawan built a madrasa at Bidar. It later split into five Deccan sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar).

concepts.title: Delhi Sultanate (1206 to 1526)
concepts.body:
Order of dynasties: Slave (Mamluk), Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi. Before them, Muhammad Ghori beat Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), after losing the first (1191).

RulerRemember for
Qutb-ud-din AibakFounder (1206); 'Lakh Baksh'; began the Qutub Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque
IltutmishCompleted Qutub Minar; silver tanka and copper jital; iqta system; group of forty nobles (Chahalgani)
Razia SultanFirst and only woman ruler of Delhi
BalbanTheory of kingship; sijda and paibos; 'blood and iron' policy
Alauddin KhiljiMarket control, branding of horses (dagh) and descriptive rolls (chehra); Alai Darwaza; Siri fort; general Malik Kafur raided the south
Ghiyasuddin TughlaqFounder of Tughlaq dynasty; built Tughlaqabad
Muhammad bin TughlaqMoved capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri); token copper currency; Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta served him
Firoz Shah TughlaqCanals; founded towns like Firozabad, Hisar, Jaunpur; brought two Ashokan pillars to Delhi
Khizr KhanFounder of Sayyid dynasty
Bahlul LodiFounder of Lodi dynasty (first Afghan dynasty)
Sikandar LodiFounded Agra (1504) and made it the capital
Ibrahim LodiLast Sultan; killed by Babur at Panipat (1526)

Writers: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri; Ziauddin Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi; Amir Khusrau ('Tuti-e-Hind', the parrot of India) served several sultans including Alauddin. The Sharqi dynasty ruled the Jaunpur Sultanate.

concepts.title: Mughals, Marathas and regional powers
concepts.body:
RulerRemember for
Babur (1526 to 1530)First Battle of Panipat 1526 (beat Ibrahim Lodi); Khanwa 1527 (Rana Sanga); memoir Baburnama in Turki
HumayunLost to Sher Shah at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540); Humayun-nama by his sister Gulbadan Begum
Sher Shah SuriSilver rupiya; rebuilt the Grand Trunk Road; tomb at Sasaram (Bihar)
Akbar (1556 to 1605)Second Battle of Panipat 1556 (Hemu); Haldighati 1576 (Maharana Pratap); mansabdari; abolished jizya; Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri; Din-i-Ilahi (1582); Buland Darwaza
JahangirChain of justice; Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri; Sir Thomas Roe came to his court (1615)
Shah JahanThe great builder: Taj Mahal, Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi, Peacock Throne
AurangzebEmpire reached its largest size; reimposed jizya (1679); died 1707
Bahadur Shah ZafarLast Mughal; exiled to Rangoon after 1857

Akbar's court: Abul Fazl (Akbarnama, Ain-i-Akbari), Faizi, Birbal, Tansen (music), Raja Todar Mal (finance minister, land revenue system), Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, Raja Man Singh.

Marathas: Shivaji was born at Shivneri (1630) and crowned at Raigad (1674); council of eight ministers (Ashtapradhan); taxes chauth and sardeshmukhi; Treaty of Purandar (1665). Peshwas: Balaji Vishwanath, Baji Rao I, Balaji Baji Rao (Third Battle of Panipat, 1761, lost to Ahmad Shah Abdali).

Regional powers: Mysore (Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan), Punjab (Maharaja Ranjit Singh, capital Lahore), Ahoms of Assam (Lachit Borphukan won the Battle of Saraighat, 1671), Nepal (Prithvi Narayan Shah unified it).

concepts.title: Bhakti, Sufi and Sikh gurus
concepts.body:
SaintRemember for
Adi ShankaracharyaAdvaita; four mathas
RamanujaVishishtadvaita
MadhvacharyaDvaita
RamanandaDevotion to Rama; disciples included Kabir and Ravidas
KabirDohas; Bijak
TulsidasRamcharitmanas (Awadhi)
SurdasSursagar; devotion to Krishna
Chaitanya MahaprabhuBengal; Krishna kirtan
Jnaneshwar, Namdev, TukaramMaharashtra (Warkari tradition)
Srimanta SankardevAssam; Ekasarana dharma; satras

Early Tamil bhakti: Alvars (devotees of Vishnu) and Nayanars (devotees of Shiva).

Sufi: the Chishti order was the most popular. Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi), Salim Chishti (Fatehpur Sikri). Other orders: Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi, Qadiri.

Sikh guruRemember for
1. Guru NanakFounder; born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib)
2. Guru AngadGurmukhi script
3. Guru Amar DasManji system; langar
4. Guru Ram DasFounded Amritsar
5. Guru Arjan DevCompiled the Adi Granth (1604); built Harmandir Sahib; executed by Jahangir (1606)
6. Guru HargobindAkal Takht
9. Guru Tegh BahadurExecuted by Aurangzeb (1675)
10. Guru Gobind SinghFounded the Khalsa (1699)

concepts.title: Europeans and British expansion
concepts.body:
Arrival: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498. Portuguese (Albuquerque took Goa, 1510), English East India Company (1600), Dutch (1602), Danes (1616), French (1664).

Battle or warYearResult
Plassey1757Clive beat Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal
Wandiwash (3rd Carnatic war)1760English beat the French
Buxar1764Beat Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II; Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave the Diwani of Bengal
Fourth Anglo-Mysore war1799Tipu Sultan killed at Srirangapatna
Anglo-Sikh wars1845 to 1849Punjab annexed (1849)
Governor-General or ViceroyLinked with
Warren HastingsFirst Governor-General of Bengal (Regulating Act 1773); Asiatic Society (1784, by William Jones)
CornwallisPermanent Settlement (1793); civil services
WellesleySubsidiary Alliance (1798); Hyderabad accepted it first
William BentinckAbolished sati (1829); first Governor-General of India (1833); English education (1835)
AucklandFirst Afghan War
DalhousieDoctrine of Lapse (Satara first, 1848); first train Bombay to Thane (1853); telegraph; Wood's Despatch (1854)
CanningRevolt of 1857; first Viceroy (1858)
LyttonVernacular Press Act (1878); Delhi Durbar (1877)
RiponLocal self-government (1882); Ilbert Bill; first regular census (1881)
DufferinCongress founded (1885)
CurzonPartition of Bengal (1905)
Minto IIMorley-Minto reforms (1909)
Hardinge IICapital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi (announced 1911)
ChelmsfordJallianwala Bagh (1919); 1919 reforms
IrwinSimon Commission; Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)
LinlithgowQuit India (1942)
MountbattenLast Viceroy; first Governor-General of free India

concepts.title: Colonial economy, 1857 and other revolts
concepts.body:
Land revenue systemWhereWho
Permanent Settlement (zamindari)Bengal, Bihar, OdishaCornwallis, 1793
Ryotwari (tax direct from the peasant)Madras and BombayThomas Munro, Alexander Read
Mahalwari (village as a unit)North-West Provinces, PunjabHolt Mackenzie

Dadabhai Naoroji explained the drain of wealth in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.

Revolt of 1857: Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore (29 March); the revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

CentreIndian leader
DelhiBahadur Shah Zafar, Bakht Khan
KanpurNana Saheb, Tantia Tope
LucknowBegum Hazrat Mahal
JhansiRani Lakshmibai
Jagdishpur (Bihar)Kunwar Singh
BareillyKhan Bahadur Khan

After it, the Government of India Act 1858 ended Company rule; Queen Victoria's Proclamation was read at Allahabad (1858).

Other revolts: Santhal (1855 to 1856, Sidhu and Kanhu); Indigo revolt (Bengal, 1859 to 1860, play Nil Darpan by Dinabandhu Mitra); Pabna (1873); Deccan riots (1875); Munda Ulgulan (Birsa Munda, 1899 to 1900); Moplah (Malabar, 1921); Rampa (Alluri Sitarama Raju, 1922 to 1924).

concepts.title: Social and religious reform
concepts.body:
OrganisationFounderYear, place
Brahmo SamajRaja Ram Mohan Roy1828, Calcutta
Prarthana SamajAtmaram Pandurang1867, Bombay
Satyashodhak SamajJyotiba Phule (wrote Gulamgiri)1873, Pune
Arya SamajDayananda Saraswati (wrote Satyarth Prakash)1875, Bombay
Theosophical SocietyMadame Blavatsky and Col. Olcott1875, New York; HQ Adyar (Madras) from 1886
Aligarh Movement (MAO College 1875)Sir Syed Ahmad KhanAligarh
Ramakrishna MissionSwami Vivekananda1897, Belur
SNDP YogamSree Narayana Guru1903, Kerala
Servants of India SocietyG.K. Gokhale1905, Pune
Self-Respect MovementE.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)1925, Tamil Nadu
  • Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar pushed for the Widow Remarriage Act, 1856.
  • Henry Vivian Derozio led the Young Bengal movement.
  • Savitribai Phule opened a girls' school in Pune (1848) with Jyotiba Phule.

concepts.title: Colonial acts, commissions and missions
concepts.body:
Act or planMain point
Regulating Act 1773Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal; Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)
Pitt's India Act 1784Board of Control
Charter Act 1813Company's trade monopoly ended (except tea and trade with China); Rs 1 lakh for education
Charter Act 1833Governor-General of India; Company became only an administrative body
Charter Act 1853Open competition for civil services
Government of India Act 1858Crown rule; Secretary of State for India
Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto)Separate electorates for Muslims
Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford)Dyarchy in provinces; two-house central legislature
Government of India Act 1935Provincial autonomy; federal court; dyarchy at the centre (never started)
Indian Independence Act 1947Two dominions, India and Pakistan
  • Simon Commission (1927, reached India 1928): seven British MPs, no Indian member, so 'Simon go back'.
  • Cripps Mission 1942; Wavell Plan and Shimla Conference 1945; Cabinet Mission 1946 (Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, A.V. Alexander); Mountbatten Plan 3 June 1947.
  • Rowlatt Act 1919 allowed arrest without trial.

concepts.title: Congress, early nationalism and revolutionaries
concepts.body:
Before Congress: East India Association (Dadabhai Naoroji, London, 1866); Indian Association (Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose, 1876).

Indian National Congress: founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume; first session at Bombay, president W.C. Bonnerjee, 72 delegates.

SessionPresidentRemember for
1886 CalcuttaDadabhai Naoroji
1887 MadrasBadruddin TyabjiFirst Muslim president
1888 AllahabadGeorge YuleFirst English president
1906 CalcuttaDadabhai NaorojiSwaraj as the goal
1907 SuratRash Behari GhoshSplit: moderates and extremists
1911 CalcuttaB.N. DharJana Gana Mana first sung
1915 BombayS.P. Sinha
1916 LucknowA.C. MazumdarLucknow Pact; the two groups reunited
1917 CalcuttaAnnie BesantFirst woman president
1924 BelgaumMahatma GandhiOnly session Gandhi presided
1925 KanpurSarojini NaiduFirst Indian woman president
1929 LahoreJawaharlal NehruPurna Swaraj resolution
1931 KarachiVallabhbhai PatelResolution on Fundamental Rights and economic policy
1938 Haripura, 1939 TripuriSubhas Chandra BoseBose resigned in 1939
  • Muslim League: 1906, Dhaka. Jinnah was called 'Quaid-i-Azam'.
  • Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905 and was annulled in 1911.
  • Home Rule Leagues (1916): Tilak and Annie Besant. Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco): Lala Har Dayal.

Revolutionaries: Khudiram Bose (Muzaffarpur, 1908); Alipore bomb case (Aurobindo Ghosh); Madan Lal Dhingra (London, 1909); Kakori train action (9 August 1925, Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan); Hindustan Republican Association (1924, Sachindranath Sanyal, who wrote Bandi Jiwan); HSRA (1928, Delhi; Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad); bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly (8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt); Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev hanged on 23 March 1931; Chittagong armoury raid (1930, Surya Sen). The Philosophy of the Bomb was written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra.

concepts.title: Gandhian era (1915 to 1947)
concepts.body:
In South Africa Gandhi formed the Natal Indian Congress (1894). He returned to India on 9 January 1915 (now Pravasi Bharatiya Divas).

YearEvent
1917Champaran Satyagraha (indigo farmers, Bihar), first satyagraha in India
1918Ahmedabad mill strike (first hunger strike) and Kheda Satyagraha
1919Rowlatt Satyagraha; Jallianwala Bagh massacre, Amritsar, 13 April (General Dyer); Tagore gave up his knighthood
1920Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement (Khilafat protested the treatment of the Ottoman Caliph of Turkey)
1922Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, 5 February); Non-Cooperation called off
1923Swaraj Party (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru)
1928Simon Commission protests; Lala Lajpat Rai died after a lathi charge; Bardoli Satyagraha made Vallabhbhai 'Sardar'
1930Dandi March (12 March to 6 April) from Sabarmati Ashram; Civil Disobedience; First Round Table Conference
1931Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference
1932Communal Award; Poona Pact (Gandhi and Ambedkar)
1940Individual Satyagraha (Vinoba Bhave first)
1942Quit India, 8 August, Gowalia Tank, Bombay: 'Do or Die'
1943Subhas Bose leads the INA; Azad Hind government at Singapore (21 October)
1944Battles of Kohima and Imphal
1946Royal Indian Navy mutiny (Bombay); Direct Action Day (16 August); interim government (2 September)

concepts.title: India after 1947
concepts.body:
• First Prime Minister: Jawaharlal Nehru. First Deputy PM and Home Minister: Sardar Patel. Last Governor-General: C. Rajagopalachari (the only Indian one).
  • Constitution in force 26 January 1950; first general elections 1951 to 1952.
  • Andhra State formed in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's fast; States Reorganisation Act 1956 (Fazl Ali Commission).
  • Panchsheel agreement with China: 1954. Goa freed: 1961. War with China: 1962.
  • War with Pakistan 1965, then the Tashkent Agreement (1966). War of 1971 created Bangladesh; Simla Agreement 1972.
  • Pokhran I (18 May 1974, 'Smiling Buddha'): PM Indira Gandhi, President V.V. Giri.
  • Emergency: 25 June 1975 to March 1977. Sikkim became a state in 1975.
  • Pokhran II (May 1998): PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee, President K.R. Narayanan.
  • Lahore bus journey (Vajpayee): February 1999. Kargil war: 1999.

varieties.name: Stone Age, Indus and Vedic
varieties.how: Learn the Indus sites as site, state or river, and one find. For Vedic questions, link each Veda and Vedanga to one word (Rig: oldest hymns, Sama: music, Kalpa: ritual).

example.q: Which Harappan site had a dockyard?
steps: Dockyard means a port city.
The Harappan port with a dockyard is Lothal in Gujarat.

varieties.name: Buddhism, Jainism and Mahajanapadas
varieties.how: Use the four places of Buddha's life in order and the council table (place, king). For Mahajanapadas, learn the capital pairs.

example.q: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held under which king?
steps: Councils: Rajagriha (Ajatashatru), Vaishali (Kalashoka), Pataliputra (Ashoka), Kashmir (Kanishka).
Fourth is Kashmir, under Kanishka.

varieties.name: Mauryas to Guptas and Harsha
varieties.how: Match each king to one book, traveller or inscription. Travellers come in fixed pairs: Megasthenes with Chandragupta Maurya, Fa-Hien with Chandragupta II, Hiuen Tsang with Harsha.

example.q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II?
steps: Fa-Hien came in the time of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
Hiuen Tsang came later, under Harsha.

varieties.name: South Indian and Deccan kingdoms
varieties.how: Link each dynasty to its capital and one temple or king. Kailasa (Ellora) is Rashtrakuta; Brihadeeswara is Chola; Mahabalipuram is Pallava.

steps: The title means 'the Chola who conquered the Ganga'.
Rajendra I led the northern campaign to the Ganga.

varieties.name: Delhi Sultanate
varieties.how: First fix the dynasty order (Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi), then one reform or building per ruler.

example.q: Who introduced the silver tanka and copper jital?
steps: Coins are linked to the early Slave dynasty.
Iltutmish issued the silver tanka and copper jital.

varieties.name: Mughals, Marathas and regional powers
varieties.how: Learn emperors in order (Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb) with one battle, book or building each. For Marathas remember Shivaji's forts and the Peshwas.

example.q: Under which emperor did the Mughal Empire reach its largest size?
steps: Akbar expanded it greatly, but Aurangzeb added the Deccan sultanates of Bijapur and Golconda.
So the peak in area was under Aurangzeb.

varieties.name: Bhakti, Sufi and Sikh gurus
varieties.how: Pair each saint with region, deity and book. Number the Sikh gurus and attach one act to each.

example.q: Who was the fifth Sikh guru?
steps: Order: Nanak, Angad, Amar Das, Ram Das, Arjan Dev.
The fifth is Guru Arjan Dev, who compiled the Adi Granth.

varieties.name: British rule, 1857 and revolts
varieties.how: Learn governors-general as name and one event. For 1857, learn centre and leader pairs. For land systems, link each to the region and the officer.

example.q: The Subsidiary Alliance was introduced by:
steps: Subsidiary Alliance started in 1798.
The Governor-General then was Lord Wellesley.

varieties.name: Social and religious reform
varieties.how: Keep a table of organisation, founder, year. Many questions only change one column, so learn them as triples.

steps: Arya Samaj: 1875, Bombay.
Founder: Swami Dayananda Saraswati, who wrote Satyarth Prakash.

varieties.name: Colonial acts and commissions
varieties.how: Learn each act by its year and one change. Nicknames help: Morley-Minto is 1909, Montagu-Chelmsford is 1919.

example.q: Which Act is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms?
steps: Morley was Secretary of State and Minto was Viceroy around 1909.
The Act is the Indian Councils Act, 1909, which gave separate electorates to Muslims.

varieties.name: National movement
varieties.how: Write the year beside each event before ordering. For sessions, learn place, year, president and why it matters.

example.q: Arrange in order: Quit India, Dandi March, Partition of Bengal, Jallianwala Bagh.
steps: Partition of Bengal 1905, Jallianwala Bagh 1919.
Dandi March 1930, Quit India 1942.
example.answer: Partition of Bengal, Jallianwala Bagh, Dandi March, Quit India

varieties.name: India after 1947
varieties.how: Learn the year of each landmark and who was PM and President then. Check terms carefully: an office holder changes mid-year.

example.q: Who was the President of India at the time of the first nuclear test at Pokhran (1974)?
steps: The test was on 18 May 1974.
V.V. Giri was President until August 1974; Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed took over after that.

tips: Buddha's four places in order of life: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar (L, B, S, K).
Delhi Sultanate order: 'Some Kings Take Steps Lightly' gives Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi.
Mughal order: 'Black Horse Always Jumps Silly Animals' gives Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb.
Three Panipat battles: 1526 (Babur), 1556 (Akbar), 1761 (Abdali). Each gap is about 30, then about 200 years.
Travellers come in pairs with kings: Megasthenes and Chandragupta Maurya, Fa-Hien and Chandragupta II, Hiuen Tsang and Harsha, Ibn Battuta and Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Thomas Roe and Jahangir.
Act nicknames follow the Viceroy: Morley-Minto 1909, Montagu-Chelmsford 1919.
For chronology questions, write the year beside each option before comparing.
traps: Harappa (Daya Ram Sahni, 1921) and Mohenjo-daro (R.D. Banerji, 1922) are often swapped.
Qutub Minar was begun by Aibak but completed by Iltutmish.
A.O. Hume founded the Congress, but W.C. Bonnerjee presided over its first session.
Annie Besant was the first woman Congress president (1917); Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president (1925).
Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal; William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India; Canning was the first Viceroy.
Pokhran I (1974) was under President V.V. Giri, not Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, who took office in August 1974.

questions.q: Who led the first excavation at Harappa in 1921?
questions.solution:
Harappa was first excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921 (under John Marshall as ASI Director-General). R.D. Banerji excavated Mohenjo-daro in 1922.
Memory hook: Harappa came first, so the first name, Sahni, goes with 1921.

questions.q: The Mughal Empire in India was founded after which battle?
questions.solution:
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526) and founded the Mughal Empire.
Memory hook: 1526: Babur's 'first' Panipat = first Mughal.

questions.q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress (1885)?
questions.solution:
The first INC session was held at Bombay in 1885 and was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee. A.O. Hume was the founder.
Memory hook: Hume founded, Bonnerjee presided.

questions.q: Which ruler adopted Buddhism after the Kalinga war?
questions.solution:
The bloodshed of the Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE) moved Ashoka to adopt Buddhism and follow Dhamma.
Memory hook: Kalinga changed Ashoka from 'Chandashoka' (fierce) to 'Dharmashoka'.

questions.q: Which Delhi Sultan shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) and also issued token currency. Both experiments failed.
Memory hook: Muhammad bin Tughlaq = 'ideas ahead of time': token money and a new capital.

questions.q: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
questions.solution:
The massacre took place at Amritsar on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day) under General Dyer, after protests against the Rowlatt Act.
Memory hook: Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala are both 1919.

questions.q:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Quit India Movement
2. Partition of Bengal
3. Dandi March
4. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
questions.solution:
Partition of Bengal 1905 → Jallianwala Bagh 1919 → Dandi March 1930 → Quit India 1942. So 2, 4, 3, 1.
Memory hook: 05 – 19 – 30 – 42: each gap grows by about a decade.

questions.q: Which pair is incorrectly matched (place — event in Buddha's life)?
questions.solution:
Kushinagar is where Buddha attained mahaparinirvana (death). Enlightenment was at Bodh Gaya.
Memory hook: L-B-S-K follows his life: born, enlightened, taught, passed away.
